claim: Generated code for netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework targets is not decorated. Every template wraps the attribute in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`. `System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute` exists in .NET Framework 4.0+ and in netstandard2.0, and it can target classes there. So the exclusion is unnecessary and breaks the criterion 'All generated code is decorated' for a large share of consumers (netstandard2.0 libraries, .NET Framework apps). The README documents the gap rather than closing it.

claim: Every opt-in emission is wrapped in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`, so a consumer project targeting netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework (net472, net48) gets no `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` on any generated formatter or resolver. `System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute` has existed since .NET Framework 4.0 and is in netstandard2.0, and it has always allowed AttributeTargets.Class. Only AttributeTargets.Assembly was added later. The guard therefore drops the attribute on targets where it compiles fine. That breaks 'all generated code is decorated' for netstandard2.0 libraries, which are the most common MessagePack consumers.
